reuse.why: Factors the rules into small SQL fragments (NO_TEMPLATE_SQL, hiddenSql) and getFixedCategoryIds, but there is no shared category-selection function, so every action still builds its own query, loop and skips.

duplication.why: The SELECT-categories query, the fixed-group skip and the income skip are repeated in setZero, set3/6/12MonthAvg and the new setLastMonthSpending, which copies the whole skeleton; copyPreviousMonth restates the hidden and template rules a third way.

placement.why: Everything stays in budget/actions.ts and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts next to its siblings with mutator(undoable(...)).

scope.why: Changes are on-topic across the four steps; the tests and release notes are proportionate.

maintainability.why: Each new exclusion so far had to be added to six actions by hand, and the hidden rule now exists as a flagged SQL fragment with a requireGroup variant plus a JS condition, so the next rule change will again touch every action.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth in budget/actions.ts ignores hiddenSql and decides hidden/group-hidden in JS, and queries templates separately with NOT NO_TEMPLATE_SQL.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden/template exclusion appears as SQL fragments in the five query-based actions and reshaped as JS set lookups and an includeHiddenCategories condition in copyPreviousMonth; setLastMonthSpending is a near copy of set3MonthAvg's skeleton.

abstraction_drift.where: hiddenSql gained includeHiddenCategories and a requireGroup option (with an early-return branch for include and a COALESCE vs strict branch); copyPreviousMonth bypasses it with its own hidden check, and the fixed/income skips are re-applied per call site rather than inside a shared selector.
